## Document
`SUP-100864-webhook-body-canonicalization-retry-signature-mismatch` — "**Webhook signature mismatch after client-side retry causes duplicated function-call side effects**" (§1, p1), a Sev1/P1 Jira support request (key `SUP-100864`, customer **BrightCart Inc.**, created `2026-03-11`, updated `2026-03-13`, reporter Aisha Patel, env `prod | us-east`).

## Symptom (§2 description, p1)
> "when their edge worker (Cloudflare) hits a transient timeout while processing our function-call callback, Redwood retries delivery… The retry contains the same pavload but the signature header (x-rw-signature) differs. BrightCart's verification rejects this retry (401) and their application performs a compensating re-processing that results in duplicate side effects."

Impact: "~0.3% of calls … (~120 duplicates)" of duplicate order confirmations.

## Root cause (§5 triage, p2)
> "Checked delivery service: initial attempt uses chunked gzip path; retry falls back to non-chunked encoding to satisfy a different upstream route. This behavior was triggered by a gateway route selection policy that aims for smaller retries."

> "**api-gateway signs the payload after compression step.** The signing call is currently invoked after the compression encoder. The retry code path triggers a different encoder instance which produced identical logical JSON but not identical bytes (spacing and … key order stable but **gzip container differences** and CRI E normalization changed raw bytes)."

> "Edge proxies (Cloudflare) have auto-decompress/inflate behavior for certain responses which can lead to the worker forwarding a slightly re-serialized body back to origin, affecting the bytes that BrightCart sees in the retry chain."

Confirmed in the repro (§6, 2026-03-11 14:40, Marco Ruiz):
> "initia[l] attempt bytes were gzipped with specific timestamp in gzip header; retry path produced a gzipped payload with **different gzip envelope metadata causing signature mismatch**. We're engaging SRE to review signing placement."

So: the signature was computed over the **post-compression transport bytes**, and the retry path re-encoded the body through a different gzip encoder / non-chunked route (plus edge auto-decompress re-serialization), so identical JSON produced different raw bytes → a different HMAC on `x-rw-signature`.

## Planned server-side fix (§7 resolution, p3)
> "Planned fix: **move signing to pre-compression canonical payload representation** so that retries that differ only by transport encoding still verify. Change set created and internal PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2197. Rollout plan: canary in staging -> canary in two prod clusters -> full rollout. Post-deploy verification script will run against BrightCart's harness. No permanent rollback planned. Follow-ups: update webhook integration docs to recommend canonicalization best-practices and add a header `x-rw-canonicalization-version` to indicate what representation was signed."

Interim customer workaround (§5 / §6, 2026-03-12): BrightCart verified HMAC over canonicalized JSON (compact serialization, sorted keys, normalized UTF-8), which "dropped duplicates to near 0, but we'd prefer the provider guarantee." SRE estimated "configuration change + canary in staging will be ready in 48 hours" (§6, 2026-03-13 08:30).

## Root cause — two independent defects behind the stale rows + 404 trace links

**Document:** `SUP-100200-console-query-cache-stale-after-api-key-rotation` — "Console cached query results and trace links resolve to previous API key after customer rotated API key" (Jira SUP-100200, Sev1/P1, org `brighthealth-ai`, us-east-1, created 2026-03-10).

**Symptom as reported (§6, p1):**
> "1) Rotate API key via the Console > API keys > Rotate for org brighthealth-ai — 2) Open Usage -> Ad-hoc Query with filter api_key: <new-key> and time range last 24h — 3) Observe that panel rows still show request_ids and trace links for requests made with old key — 4) Click a trace link -> Console opens trace URL and shows 404 or a trace page with request_id that predates rotation"

**Why it happens — the hypothesis in §8 (investigation_notes, p2):**
> "Two independent issues: (1) Console frontend sometimes reads from legacy cache prefix v1 which is keyed by api_key_id and remains stale post-rotation, (2) indexing migration that would remap historical requests to the org-level view hasn't been run for this customer's partition, so trace anchors reference old api_key values and the live trace lookup uses new key leading to 404s."

Supporting SRE finding (§8, p2, Diego 03/10):
> "Examined cache key format in cache-service. cache-key included api_key_id in v1 but v2 rollout switched to org_id. Observation: rotation job updates api_key table but does not trigger cache invalidation for entries keyed by api_key_id in legacy caches. Some panels still reading from legacy cache prefix (v2 migration not complete across all pods)."

So: the rotation job never emits a cache-invalidation event, panels still hitting the legacy `v1` prefix keyed on the *old* `api_key_id` keep serving pre-rotation rows (hence old request IDs), and because the per-org indexing remap hadn't run for this partition, the stored trace anchors still point at the old key while the live trace lookup queries the new key → 404. Browser cache was ruled out (incognito repro gave the same results, §9).

## Immediate mitigation applied by Support/SRE before the fix shipped

From §9 (actions_taken) and §11 (workaround, p2):
- **Manual legacy-cache flush:** "03/11 02:32 UTC - SRE manually flushed legacy cache prefix for brighthealth-ai on redis-cluster-prod-3 (keys matching 'v1:org:brighthealth-ai:*'). This momentarily allowed new queries to surface correct request_ids for new key."
- **Emergency feature flag to bypass the Console cache:** "Support (Aisha) 2026-03-11T09:30Z: Enabled emergency feature flag to bypass console cache for orgs with rotation events. Not ideal long-term but reduces surface for 404s." — §11: "Admin/Support flushed legacy cache prefixes for the customer's redis shard and enabled **ff/console/rotation-cache-bypass** which forces live index reads for orgs with an API key rotation in the last 24h."
- **Customer-side cache-busting workaround:** "Customer can also add a dummy query parameter to bust console cache (e.g., `?bust=1`) for ad-hoc queries until fix is rolled out."

**Effect:** "BrightHealth AI (Customer) 2026-03-11T19:05Z: Verified after guidance; majority of links correct now," but "a small subset (approx 0.8%) remain 404ing."

**The proper fix that later shipped (§13, resolution_plan, p3):** "Short term: Complete per-org cache flush and finish the indexing remap and remediation script (Sana). Medium term: Update rotation workflow to emit cache-invalidation events and add automated migration verification (Diego/Sana)... Deploy fix: patch indexing job to tolerate malformed legacy records and run migration across affected partitions (target: 2026-03-15)." (The 03/11 migration run on partition 42 had partial failures because some legacy `api_key` records lacked a valid `org_id`.)

**Concise answer:** The rotation job updates the `api_key` table but emits no cache invalidation, so Console panels still reading the legacy `v1` cache prefix (keyed by the old `api_key_id`) keep returning pre-rotation request IDs; and because the per-org indexing remap hadn't run for that partition, trace anchors still reference the old key while live trace lookup uses the new key, producing 404s. Before the real fix, Support/SRE manually flushed the org's legacy cache prefixes on `redis-cluster-prod-3` and flipped the emergency flag `ff/console/rotation-cache-bypass` (forcing live index reads for orgs with a rotation in the last 24h), plus told the customer to append `?bust=1` to ad-hoc queries — which fixed most links but left ~0.8% still 404ing.

## 1. Triggers / conditions for enabling region fallback (2025-03-03 incident)

**Document:** `2025-03-03-eu-west-capacity-shortage-region-fallback` · §6 "Mitigation details" (chunk `ecv1_420f4095…e9ef`, p1)

> \* Primary region: eu-west-1
> \* Fallback region: us-east-1
> **\* Triggers: saturation > 90% OR 503 rate > 0.5%**
> **\* Eligibility: routes not marked "data_residency_strict"**

The documented thresholds were **saturation > 90% OR 503 error rate > 0.5%**, and the fallback route pair was eu-west-1 → us-east-1.

The §5 "Timeline (UTC)" chunk (`ecv1_0cc01aa8…44b1`, p1) shows the thresholds actually firing:

> \* 09:42: Capacity alert: available_gpu_count < 5 in eu-west-1 pool rw-a100-eu-01.
> \* 09:48: Saturation exceeded 95% and queue wait climbed > 400ms.
> \* 09:51: Mitigation: enabled *region fallback* for "chat-default" and "embeddings-default" where customer policy allows cross-region.
> \* 09:54: Router began directing overflow to us-east-1 for eligible traffic.
> \* 10:23: Added 8 GPUs to eu-west-1 pool; disabled region fallback after stabilization.

Root cause (§7, chunk `ecv1_57e2c132…d44a`): "A delayed GPU delivery + slow provisioning left the eu-west-1 pool below the forecasted headroom for a scheduled customer load test."

## 2. Traffic excluded from the fallback

**Routes marked `data_residency_strict` were excluded** — fallback eligibility was limited to "routes not marked 'data_residency_strict'" (§6), and the router only carried "eligible traffic" (§3 summary: "activating *automatic region fallback* (eu-west-1 -> us-east-1) for eligible routes"; §8: "Region fallback prevented a full outage for eligible traffic"). Fallback was applied only to "chat-default" and "embeddings-default" **"where customer policy allows cross-region"** (§5). Conversely, §4 Impact notes only "7 Hosted orgs and 1 Dedicated tenant **with optional cross-region allowance enabled**" were in scope.

## 3. What counts as "customer content" under the region pinning policy

**Document:** `adr-021-region-pinning-enforcement-boundaries` · §2, "### 1) Definition: 'Customer content'" (p1)

> "For the purposes of region pinning enforcement, **customer content** includes any data that could revea[r] or reconstruct customer-provided or model-produced content."

> "**Customer content (MUST remain within pinned region(s))**"
> \* Prompt / messages / input text (including system prompts provided by customer)
> \* Tool/function call arguments provided by customer
> \* Uploaded documents or retrieved passages (RAG payloads) provided by customer
> \* Model outputs (including partial streaming tokens)
> \* Embeddings input text and embeddings vectors derived from customer text
> \* Rerank inputs (candidate passages) and rerank outputs derived from those passages
> \* Any derived artifacts that can reconstruct content (e.g., token logs, decoded segments, sampled prompt fragments)
> \* Any debug payloads that include raw request/response bodies
> \* Fine-tuning / adapter payloads if routed through Hosted API pathways (not in scope for v1 feature, but classification applies)

Notes in the same section: "Whether content includes PII is not determinative; **all prompts/outputs are treated as sensitive content**" and "'Derived' includes transformations (tokenization, embedding vectors, compression) if they are computed from customer text/output."

The customer-facing FAQ (`data-residency-enforcement-faq` · §2, p1) states the same boundary: "**Customer content** — Inputs and outputs of inference and closely associated content-bearing artifacts, including (non-exhaustive): Prompts/messages, uploaded text, tool/function arguments that include customer data; Model outputs/completions; Embeddings payloads."

**Policy tie-back:** ADR-021 makes residency a hard constraint — "Cross-region fallback is **disabled by default** for pinned traffic… Capacity-based routing must not override residency constraints" (§2, p2), and "'Fail open' to a non-allowed region is prohibited" (§2, p4). The FAQ likewise: "**Cross-region fallback is disabled by default** when residency pinning is enabled. Fallback is only permitted **within the allowed region set**."

---

**Concise answer:** Fallback (eu-west-1 → us-east-1) was enabled when **saturation exceeded 90% OR the 503 rate exceeded 0.5%** (in practice: `available_gpu_count < 5` alert at 09:42, then saturation >95% with queue wait >400ms at 09:48). **Traffic on routes marked `data_residency_strict` was excluded** — only routes where customer policy allowed cross-region (chat-default, embeddings-default) failed over. Under the region pinning policy, "customer content" is any data that could reveal or reconstruct customer-provided or model-produced content: prompts/messages/input text (incl. customer system prompts), tool/function-call arguments, uploaded documents and retrieved RAG passages, model outputs including partial streaming tokens, embeddings inputs/vectors, rerank inputs and outputs, derived reconstructable artifacts (token logs, decoded segments, prompt fragments), debug payloads containing raw request/response bodies, and fine-tuning/adapter payloads.

## Incident located: `SUP-63219` — "rbac policy 'not_in' operator fallthrough grants unexpected access when claim missing in private deployment"

**Doc:** `SUP-63219-rbac-policy-not_in-operator-absent-claim-fallthrough-grants-unexpected-access-in-private` (Jira/customer-support, P1 / Sev1, customer **Atlas Retail**, private VPC, `prod-us-east`, related incident `INC-2026-0313-07`, observation window **2026-03-12 22:30 – 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC**).

### The bug (symptom)
§2 (p1):
> "Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer provided a minimal policy that allows action if `user.entitlements not_in ["admin", "superuser"]` 2) Send request with JWT that omits the 'entitlements' claim altogether 3) Call to `/admin/config` returns 200 and allowed instead of denied. … **Observed behavior: Policy evaluator treats missing claim in 'not_in' as a non-match that bypasses exclusion, resulting in grant.**"

§4 log evidence:
> `2026-03-13T00:11:45Z authz-eval INFO allow user=svc-ordering token_kid=abcd1234 trace=trace-20260313-34b9 expr='user.entitlements not_in ["admin","superuser"]' claim=ABSENT` followed by `proxy INFO request forwarded route=/admin/config status=200`

### Root cause in the policy evaluator
§6 (`investigation`, p2):
> "AuthZ engine's expression runtime performs 'not_in' by iterating subject values and checking membership against target list; **when claim is absent the evaluator treats subject as a single empty string value leading to membership checks that return false and overall expression evaluating to true.**"
> "**Root cause hypothesis: backward-compatible change in the policy-eval library (v2.14.0) introduced value coercion for absent claims.** Related PR suspected: … commit `5f7e2b3`. Impact surface: Private deployments that rely on omission semantics for exclusion policies. Risk: Moderate-high for private customers using exclusion-based RBAC."

## Answer

**Cause:** the canary's rollout config set `fallback_policy.type = "sticky"` with `preferred_variant = "latest"` instead of an explicit stable tag. Because the canary itself also carried the label `latest`, the sticky fallback resolved that label to the *newest* tag — i.e. right back onto the failing canary in eu‑west‑1 — so sticky fallback pinned requests to the broken variant instead of the stable `stable-quantized` one (stickiness was bound to the variant *label*, not to a stable region/variant). A secondary contributor was `sticky_ttl_sec = 3600`, far too long, which made transient drains sticky and blocked re-routing during mitigation.

**Mitigations:** pause the rollout and freeze canary traffic (`redwood rollout pause --id rlt-9a3f --region eu-west-1`); patch the fallback policy from `sticky`/`latest` to `forced_variant: stable-quantized`; cordon/drain the eu‑west‑1 canary pods; lower the sticky TTL (target ≤300s for canaries); enable a temporary per-region circuit-breaker (`error_rate=0.05 duration=300s --action=force-stable`); plus follow-up hardening — runtime guard so fallback can never resolve to an in-flight canary tag (RT‑4729), platform validation rejecting `sticky` + `latest` (PLAT‑2310), and runbook update (DOC‑889). 5xx dropped 18% → 1.2% within 3 minutes.

**1) Required fields in each shadow probe telemetry record**

The authoritative contract for this scenario is *Edge Shadow Telemetry Contract for Private and Dedicated Evaluations* (`edge-shadow-telemetry-contract-2026`), which "defines the telemetry contract and operational workflow required to run edge and private shadow evaluations against customer-managed (Private) and Dedicated pools" (§3, p1). Under "Telemetry payload spec (minimal required fields)" it states: "Each shadow probe record must contain the following top-level fields (string or numeric types only):" (§6, p1), and lists:

- `probe_id` — unique id for the probe run (uuid)
- `tenant_id` — hashed tenant id (sha256 hex) or obfuscated alias; "raw customer IDs MUST NOT be sent outside the private boundary unless agreed"
- `deployed_model` — model name + version (e.g., `redwood-7b-v2-quant8`)
- `deployment_variant` — one of `[hosted, dedicated, private]`
- `quant_profile` — label of quant profile used (e.g., `q8_fast_fp16_fallback`)
- `hardware_tag` — e.g., `a100-40gb`, `t4-16gb`, `edge-x86-32g`
- `prompt_family` — short token describing probe set (e.g., `billing_faq_anchors_v3`)
- `seed_context_hash` — sha1 of the prompt/context after canonicalization (for deduping; non-reversible)
- `latency_ms` — observed end-to-end request latency in ms (int)
- `tokens_input` — token count of input (int)
- `tokens_generated` — token count generated (int)
- `top_level_metrics` — comma-separated string of key metrics, e.g., `coherence:0.82,hallucination:0.03,embed_cos_sim:0.67`
- `error_code` — empty string or standardized code (see appendix error-code-table)
- `timestamp_utc` — ISO8601 timestamp

**2) Run-lifecycle telemetry events the evaluator must emit**

The evaluator-sidecar contract (`evaluator-sidecar-telemetry-contract-2025`) — the integration pattern for the sidecar that "runs alongside production model endpoints (hosted, dedicated, or private)" and "enables private deployments to run meaningful evals without shipping raw customer data off-cluster" — specifies in its "Telemetry contract (schema)" section (§7, p1):

> "All telemetry events MUST be emitted as JSON objects matching the fields below. Event types: **probe_request, probe_result, evaluator_health, fallback_action, quant_metric**. Agents must attach a consistent trace_id for cross-correlation."

So the evaluator must emit those five event types, all as JSON, correlated by a consistent `trace_id`. The same document's §6 notes the sidecar's responsibility to "Emit standardized telemetry events to the local agent/collector and the central eval ingestion endpoint" and to "Apply local fallback policies (e.g., disable quantized variant for failing slices) if configured" — which is what the `fallback_action` event records.

**Note on a related but distinct schema:** `telemetry-led-probe-feedback-and-onboarding-contract-2026` (§7, p1) also names "The evaluator-sidecar is the primary emitter" and lists a different required-field set for probes submitted to the central eval mesh (`probe_id`, `probe_version`, `tenant_id`, `run_id`, `timestamp_utc`, `model`, `seq_len_input`, `seq_len_output`, `tokens_consumed`, `latency_ms_p50`, `latency_ms_p95`, `kv_cache_hit`, `failure_code`, plus `response_stability_score` and `telemetry_schema_version: "v1"`). That document does not define run-lifecycle event types, and its field list is for eval-mesh probe submission rather than the private shadow-probe record, so the private-deployment answer above follows the edge/private contract plus the sidecar event list.

## Answer

**Root cause of the signature verification failures**

The failures were not caused by invalid artifact signatures but by **corrupt/stale public key material on the release runners, produced by the key-rotation publishing pipeline**. Per §12 `root_cause` (p2) of `INT-23789-release-gpg-verification-failure-after-key-rotation`:

> *"Partial: key rotation publishing pipeline returned truncated key blobs due to improper handling of chunked transfer from internal keyserver, combined with gpg version mismatches across runner images leading to inconsistent import/verification results."*

Investigation notes (§10, p2) pin the mechanism:
- *"Keyserver response on 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC returned a header 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' causing our naive keysync microservice to truncate key exports; this produced a malformed pubkey blob on some runners."*
- *"Reproduced locally by fetching key export via existing keysync service: got truncated payload resulting in 'invalid packet' on import."*
- *"Verified public key published at keys.redwood.internal shows fingerprint that does not match ABCD1234; shows new key EFGH5678"* — while the signer `artifact-signer@build-01` was still signing with gpg 2.2.20 and key-id `ABCD1234`, and some runners kept outdated cached keyrings trusting the old fingerprint.
- *"Compared signature packets with pktdump: some signatures created by gpg 2.3.x include new signature subpacket format that gpg 2.2.20 accepts but older container images have varying behavior."*

Symptom chain (§3, §7, p1): after the `team-release@gpg` rotation on 2026-03-09, `gpg --verify` exited 2 with `BAD_SIGNATURE` / `invalid packet (ctb=0x0)` at the `verify-signature` step, aborting all release promotion jobs in prod-us-east and blocking the hotfix (§4).

**Immediate operational mitigations that unblocked hotfix promotions**
1. **Temporary allowlist of the previous key on selected prod runners** — *"Ops pulled the previous GPG public key from backup and added it to a temporary allowlist on three runners (release-runner-prod-03/04/07) — pipelines for those runners succeeded for a single build (hotfix candidate)."* (§9)
2. **Temporary rollback of the signing host to the previous key** — §13: *"Partial mitigation applied: temporary rollback of signing host to previous key for immediate hotfix, and targeted keyring refresh jobs run on three canary runners."* Confirmed by Sinead O'Neill (Release Eng, 2026-03-11 03:10): *"We're rolling back signer to previous key for next 6 hours to allow patching."* Security-gated by Ben Walters (2026-03-10 12:41): *"Please do not re-enable old key broadly without approval. We need a signed rollback decision in Confluence and ephemeral audit note."* A temporary fallback-verification window to the previous key for releases created in the next 24 hours likewise required Risk approval.
3. **Targeted keyring force-refresh / force-import jobs** pulling an explicit public key file from S3 — Ravi Patel (2026-03-11 09:05): *"Applied force-import job to release-runner-prod-03/04/07; verified pipeline pass for hotfix candidate. Planning broader keyring refresh tomorrow morning in low-traffic window."*
4. **gpg version bump on a canary runner** — *"Bumped the runner container gpg package from 2.2.20 -> 2.3.8 on a canary runner"* (§9), after *"Spun up canary runner and validated gpg version mismatch"* (2026-03-10 10:02).

**Permanent fix being rolled out** (§13 next steps, §14 `follow_up_actions`, p2): patch the keysync service to handle chunked transfer correctly and *"validate Content-Length/Checksums on key export"*; *"schedule controlled rollout of new public key to all runners with checksum verification"*; *"Add key fingerprint validation step to CI key import job"*; *"Upgrade runner base image gpg to 2.3.x in next CI image release"* / standardize gpg in runner images; publish the rollback decision and timeline in Confluence. Emily Chen requested the post-mortem on 2026-03-12 08:30 with runbook updates for keyserver transfer-encoding validation and key-export checksums. The ticket remained **In Progress** as of its last update (2026-03-12), so fleet-wide completion is not confirmed in this record.

> "caroline_sre: confirm. Looks like the client header crosses the NGINX buffer and triggers early abort. **For streaming, this abort happens before request body processed so stream gets 502 mid-response.**"

## Server-side mitigation deployed

> "deploy-bot: deployment request created: **ENGOPS-4392 -> add edge header-filter rule to drop X-User-Meta > 4096 bytes; targeted canary in eu1 in 30m.**"
> "ben_eng: quick scan — some tenant-routing used X-Tenant-ID & X-Model-Meta, **not X-User-Meta. This header is app-level and not used by routing. safe to filter.**"
> "caroline_sre: started canary for ENGOPS-4392 on eu1, 5% traffic... canary looks good after 20m. customer -> no 502s in last 15m for previously failing trace ids."
> "daniel_customer: confirmed! no failures in the last 30m, thank you."
> "caroline_sre: long-term: add header-size defensive trimming at edge for untrusted headers used for telemetry. For hosted customers, dropping oversized arbitrary headers is low risk."
> "ben_eng: scheduled follow-up ticket to **increase midproxy header buffers as permanent mitigation** in next maintenance window: INFRA-1287."

## Answer

- **Root cause:** the ~12KB base64 `X-User-Meta` header exceeded the midproxy NGINX header/proxy buffer (default `proxy_buffer_size` 8k). NGINX logged "client sent too large header or cookie" / "request header too large" and aborted the upstream connection instead of returning a 4xx; the fronting Envoy at the EU (eu1) edge then surfaced that reset as **502 "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"**. On streaming HTTP/2 generate calls the abort happened before the body was processed, so streams failed intermittently (~10%) mid-response.
- **Mitigation deployed:** a server-side **edge header-filter rule (ENGOPS-4392) that drops the `X-User-Meta` header when it exceeds 4096 bytes (4KB)**, canaried on eu1 (5% traffic) — it was verified safe because routing uses `X-Tenant-ID`/`X-Model-Meta`, not `X-User-Meta`. 502s stopped for the previously failing traces; a follow-up ticket (INFRA-1287) was opened to permanently raise the midproxy header buffers.

> - - The runner always constructs and passes an explicit `torch.Generator` for generation, derived from a root seed plus a stable per-example index."

> "## Deterministic decoding mode (required behavior)

> - - `do_sample = false`
> - - `temperature = 0.0`
> - - `top_k = 1`
> - - `top_p = 1.0`
> - - `num_beams = 1` (unless the suite explicitly tests beam search)
> - - Explicit generator passed into generation APIs
> - - Stable batching order (no data-loader shuffling; stable sort by example_id)"

> "- - `--seed SEED` : sets the root seed"

## Redwood Inference's end-to-end secret/credential rotation process

The process is defined by a **policy layer** (`secret-management-standard`) plus three execution runbooks (`production-secret-rotation-runbook`, `emergency-rotation-during-incident`, `post-rotation-verification-checklist`) and an emergency-access policy (`break-glass-and-emergency-access`).

### 1. Governing standard — scope, storage, tiers, cadence
`secret-management-standard` §Overview (p1): *"This standard defines how Redwood Inference stores, uses, and rotates **secrets and credentials** for production services. The objective is to reduce the blast radius of credential compromise and ensure rotation is routine and low-risk."*

- **Definitions** (§Definitions, p1): *Secret* = "any value that grants access (API keys, database passwords, service tokens, signing keys, OAuth client secrets, private keys)"; *Credential rotation* = "replacing a secret with a new value and updating all consumers"; *Emergency rotation* = "accelerated rotation performed due to suspected compromise or active incident."
- **Approved storage** (§Approved storage systems, p1): "Redwood Vault (primary)" or "Cloud KMS/HSM-backed secret store where required by compliance". Prohibited: "plaintext in Git repositories", "plaintext in Confluence/Google Docs", "long-lived secrets in CI logs", "hard-coded values in container images".
- **Classification** (§Secret classification, p1): Tier 0 = "root/admin credentials, signing keys, KMS master operations"; Tier 1 = "service-to-service auth tokens, database credentials, message bus credentials"; Tier 2 = "third-party API keys with limited scopes, internal read-only tokens".
- **Minimum cadence** (§Rotation requirements, p1): "Tier 0: every **30 days** + after any personnel change impacting privileged access / Tier 1: every **90 days** / Tier 2: every **180 days**".
- **Immediate rotation is required if** (p1): "a secret is exposed in logs, tickets, or a public repository", "a workstation is compromised and had access to Vault tokens", "an access anomaly is detected in audit logs".
- **Design requirements** (p1): "Support dual-read / dual-verify where possible (accept old+new for a bounded window)", "Prefer short-lived tokens derived from an identity provider", "Avoid single shared credentials across unrelated services".
- **Logging/audit** (p1): "Access to Tier 0 and Tier 1 secrets must be auditable (requester identity, time, action)"; "Rotation events must be recorded in a change record (or incident record for emergency)."
- **Ownership** (§Ownership, p2): "Secret owner is the owning service team; Security sets minimum standards and reviews exceptions. On-call teams may execute emergency rotations but must follow the break-glass process."
- **Exceptions** (p2) require "rationale and compensating controls", "expiration date", "Security approval".

### 2. Planned rotation — Production Secret Rotation Runbook
§Purpose (p1): *"This runbook provides a repeatable procedure for rotating production secrets used by Redwood services. It covers both planned and emergency rotation patterns."*

- **Preconditions** (§4, p1): "Identify the secret name/path and all consumers (see Credential Dependencies page)"; "Confirm rotation type: planned vs emergency"; "Ensure appropriate access (normal approvals or break-glass for emergencies)."
- **Pattern A: Dual-valid window (preferred)** (§5–6, p1) — "Use when the downstream system can accept two credentials temporarily (e.g., JWT verification keys, API keys with overlap)":
  1. Generate new credential. 2. "Store new credential in Vault under a new version (do not delete old)." 3. "Update consumers to read the latest version and accept both old+new if applicable." 4. Deploy changes. 5. "Observe auth success metrics for at least 30 minutes." 6. "Disable old credential at the issuer (or mark old as deprecated)." 7. "Remove old credential from Vault after the deprecation window (default 7 days unless otherwise specified)."
- **Pattern B: Cutover (use with caution)** (§7–8, p1) — "Use when only one credential can be active (e.g., some database passwords)": schedule a short change window with on-call coverage; reduce autoscaling noise; generate new credential but don't activate; "Apply credential change at the issuer (DB/IdP/provider)"; "Immediately update Vault with new value"; "Restart/redeploy all consumers"; "Validate service health; if failures persist, roll back or restore prior credential if possible."
- **Documentation requirements** (§11, p1): "Planned rotation: create a change record with impacted services, steps, and validation. Emergency rotation: document in incident timeline and follow up with a postmortem action list."
- **Common secret types** (§12, p2): Postgres — "prefer dual-user approach (create new user, grant perms, migrate consumers, remove old user)"; third-party API keys — "keep overlap window, update key scopes to minimum required"; signing keys — "rotate via key ring; services must trust both keys during overlap."

### 3. Emergency rotation
**Runbook §Emergency rotation procedure** (§9–10, p1), "If compromise is suspected": "1. Open an incident and declare emergency rotation. 2. Use break-glass if required; minimize secret exposure in chat (never paste secret values). 3. Rotate the highest-risk secrets first (Tier 0 then Tier 1). 4. For widely shared credentials, consider temporarily disabling the credential before cutover if safe. 5. After containment, enumerate all downstream consumers and rotate any derived tokens."

**`emergency-rotation-during-incident`** §Goal (p1): *"Provide a coordinated process for rotating secrets quickly during an active incident (suspected compromise or immediate containment need)."*
- **Decision — rotate now?** Triggers: "credible evidence of secret exposure", "vendor reports compromised credentials", "attacker has access to systems that can read secrets", "abnormal access patterns consistent with key misuse". Guardrail: "If impact is purely availability (no compromise signal), prefer standard mitigation first; emergency rotation adds risk."
- **Roles**: "Incident Commander (IC): authorizes emergency rotation and prioritizes which secrets first"; "Ops/SRE: executes changes and monitors service health"; "Service owners: update consumers and validate functionality"; "Security: advises on scope and evidence capture".
- **Procedure**: declare in the incident channel ("Emergency secret rotation in progress", names/paths only); "Link the break-glass event (if used) and ensure audit logging is on"; rotation order "Tier 0 first (signing keys, privileged service tokens)" then "Tier 1 next (DB creds, message bus creds, third-party keys with broad scopes)"; per secret — "confirm consumers from the Credential Dependencies inventory / choose rotation pattern (dual-valid if available; cutover otherwise) / rotate issuer-side credential / update Vault/secret store / restart/redeploy consumers as required / validate per-service health"; "If failures persist beyond 10 minutes and customer impact is increasing, pause and reassess: rollback vs continue rotation"; "Record exact timestamps for issuer-side change and consumer rollouts."
- **Communications**: "Do not paste secret values in Slack, tickets, or docs"; "If customer impact is expected, coordinate with Support for messaging."
- **After-action**: "File a post-incident review item that lists rotated secrets, impacted services, and any follow-up rotations needed (derived tokens, cached credentials)"; "Ensure break-glass access is revoked."

**Break-glass controls** (`break-glass-and-emergency-access`, p1): permitted only when "there is an active customer-impacting incident, or … a credible suspicion of credential compromise requiring immediate containment, or an operational safety issue requires urgent mitigation and normal approvals are too slow". Controls: "Access is time-bound to **60 minutes** (extensions require explicit SRE + Security approval)"; "All actions must be logged (audit trails cannot be disabled)"; "Any secret retrieved via break-glass must be treated as compromised and rotated if exposure scope is uncertain." Required steps: open/link incident → announce break-glass use in channel → acquire role via approved workflow → "Execute the minimum set of actions necessary" → "Revoke break-glass role immediately after use" → post-incident summary of secrets rotated and services touched. "Security reviews all break-glass events weekly."

### 4. Post-rotation verification
`post-rotation-verification-checklist` §Purpose (p1): *"This checklist defines the required verification steps after rotating production secrets to ensure all consumers have updated and service health is stable."* Execute in order: (1) confirm consumer rollout — "Verify all services that consume the rotated secret have been restarted/redeployed if required", "no straggler instances on old revisions"; (2) "Watch for 30 minutes minimum (60 minutes for Tier 0)" on "401/403 rates for service-to-service calls", "database authentication failures", "third-party provider invalid key errors", "sudden increases in retry rate"; (3) canary critical journeys — "Hosted API chat completion (streaming and non-streaming)", "embeddings endpoint", "console login (if SSO secrets rotated)", "model registry artifact fetch"; (4) audit checks — "Confirm audit logs show only expected actors accessed the secret during rotation window", "Confirm break-glass access (if used) has been revoked"; (5) decommission — "disable the old credential at the issuer", "confirm no consumer is still using it", "remove old secret version from Vault after the defined window". **Exit criteria**: all consumers updated, error rates at baseline, no unexplained auth failures, old credential disabled or scheduled for disablement. On problems: "Identify the failing dependency", "Check the dependency inventory for missing consumers", and "If customer impact is increasing, revert or temporarily re-enable the old credential where possible and then retry rotation with tighter coordination."

**In short:** classify the secret into Tier 0/1/2 → store only in Vault/KMS-HSM → rotate on a 30/90/180-day cadence (or immediately on exposure/anomaly) → follow the runbook's dual-valid (preferred) or cutover pattern with change records → for suspected compromise, declare an incident, use time-boxed break-glass, rotate Tier 0 then Tier 1, rotate derived tokens → verify with the post-rotation checklist (30/60-min observation, canaries, audit review) → disable/remove the old credential after the deprecation window (default 7 days) → close out with a change record or postmortem action list.

## SOP: Enabling customer‑managed audit log export (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

The corpus contains a complete, cross‑referenced SOP set: a CS/Support intake SOP, a mandatory Security controls page, three per‑mode runbooks, an architecture/operational‑model page, and a retention‑responsibility policy. Below is the end‑to‑end procedure with the exact supporting language.

---

### 0. Scope (what is being enabled)

> "This page defines the **mandatory security controls** and **approval gates** for enabling **customer-managed audit log export** from Redwood Inference to customer-controlled cloud storage (e.g., S3/GCS/Azure Blob) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments." — `customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2

In scope: "Export of **platform audit logs** (auth events, RBAC changes, API key lifecycle, console/admin actions, private control-plane actions)." Out of scope: "Model inference payload logging (prompt/completion content). That remains disabled by default and requires a separate data logging exception." (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2)

> "This SOP describes how Customer Success (CS) and Support intake, scope, and coordinate **customer-managed audit log export** requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments." — `audit-log-export-request-intake` §2

---

### 1. Required prerequisites

**Customer‑side (all modes)** — from the intake SOP and the mode runbooks:
- Destination exists and is encrypted: "Customer has completed destination setup (bucket/container created, encryption enabled)." (`hosted-audit-log-export-enablement` §2); "Customer has created the destination bucket/container and provided identity configuration." (`dedicated-audit-log-export-customer-setup` §2); "Customer has created a destination bucket/container and configured encryption and retention." (`private-audit-log-export-configuration` §2)
- Private version gate: "Customer has deployed Redwood Private version that includes `audit-export-connector` (Private bundle v2.8.0+)." (`private-audit-log-export-configuration` §2)
- Identity method chosen: "AWS assume-role / IRSA / GCP workload identity / Azure workload identity" (`audit-log-export-request-intake` §2)

**Ticket preconditions (Hosted)** — "An internal-support Jira ticket exists and includes: customer company + org_id; deployment mode: Hosted; destination type: S3/GCS/Azure Blob; destination identifiers (bucket/container, prefix, region); auth method (assume-role / workload identity); Security approval comment" (`hosted-audit-log-export-enablement` §2)

**Security control requirements that must pass** (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2):
1. **Data classification** — "Audit logs are classified as **Customer-Sensitive Metadata**"; "Audit logs must **not** include request bodies or model outputs."
2. **Encryption** — "At rest: the customer destination must be configured with server-side encryption"; "In transit: TLS 1.2+ is required for any HTTPS endpoints"; "S3: SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS (customer preference)"; "GCS: Google-managed keys or CMEK"; "Azure: Microsoft-managed keys or CMK"; "Redwood-side staging (if used by the connector) must be encrypted at rest using Redwood-managed KMS."
3. **Least privilege** — "Hosted and Dedicated exports must use **assume-role / workload identity** patterns; no long-lived customer keys stored in Redwood"; the role "must only permit: write/put to a specific bucket/container prefix" and "list only if required by the connector health checks"; "Policies must be reviewed by Security for correctness."
4. **Network/allowlisting** — "**PrivateLink / private endpoints are preferred** when available"; "Public endpoints are allowed only if authenticated and protected with least-privilege credentials"; "For Private deployments, outbound egress must be constrained by the customer (preferred) or by Redwood (if Redwood-managed networking is in scope)."
5. **Retention/deletion** — "Default recommended destination retention: **90 days** (unless the customer requires more)"; "If the customer requests retention < 30 days, note it in the request but it is allowed"; "If the customer requests retention > 1 year, Customer Success must confirm contract language supports it and that the customer understands storage cost/ownership."
6. **Logging about logging** — the platform must emit events for "export enabled/disabled", "destination changes (bucket/container/prefix)", "auth/role changes used by the connector", "delivery failures and retries", visible "in Redwood internal dashboards and retrievable for incident response."

**Private‑specific MUSTs** (`private-audit-log-export-requirements` §5): "**No long-lived static credentials** (access keys) are permitted for audit log export"; "Export auth MUST be via short-lived identity (AWS AssumeRole / GCP Workload Identity Federation)"; "Exported objects MUST be encrypted at rest"; "Exporter MUST provide *at-least-once delivery*"; "Exporter MUST support customer-controlled retention via bucket lifecycle policies"; "Exporter MUST produce operational logs/metrics that allow the customer to detect delivery gaps"; schema "MUST include: `event_time`, `actor_id`, `action`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `result`, and a stable `event_id`". Security's stance: "Non-negotiable: no static keys; use AssumeRole/WIF only." (`INT-883-private-audit-log-export-to-customer-object-storage` §8)

---

### 2. Intake and security approvals (gates)

**Step 1 — Create the internal‑support Jira ticket** (`audit-log-export-request-intake` §2): "Project: internal-support; Issue type: Support Request; Priority guidance: P2 for standard requests / P1 if tied to a customer audit deadline within 14 days / P0 only if this blocks a live incident response obligation." Collect: "Customer company; Deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private; Regions in use; Desired sink: S3 | GCS | Azure Blob; Destination details: bucket/container name, prefix, destination region; Identity method: AWS assume-role / IRSA, GCP workload identity, Azure workload identity; Operational contact + escalation contact; Retention intent (customer-owned); Target date (if tied to an audit)."

**Gate A — Customer request validation (Customer Success + Support)**; required before Security review: "customer company + deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)", "target cloud + region", "desired log categories (standard only unless exception)", "retention intent", "contact for incident notifications" (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2).

**Gate B — Security review (required for all modes)**: "Security must approve before any production enablement"; "Assign Security reviewer and request approval per the Security controls page. Attach destination policy snippets and encryption confirmation." Required evidence: "Destination policy snippet (IAM policy / role trust policy / workload identity binding); Confirmation of encryption at rest on destination; Proof of ownership (account/subscription/project identifiers); For Private: network diagram or egress policy statement." Reviewer checks: "destination configuration meets encryption and least privilege requirements; any cross-region delivery is evaluated; no inference payload logging is included." **Approval artifact**: "Jira internal-support ticket must include a Security comment: **'Approved for enablement'** with reviewer name + date." (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2; `audit-log-export-request-intake` §2)

**Gate C — Privacy/Legal check (conditional)**: "Required if any of the following are true: customer requests cross-region export that changes data residency guarantees; customer requests inclusion of user email addresses or other PII fields beyond standard audit schema; contract includes bespoke data residency clauses / customer contract includes bespoke audit log clauses." Cross‑region is allowed only when "1) Legal confirms it does not violate contractual residency terms, 2) Security confirms threat model is acceptable, 3) Customer acknowledges increased failure modes and latency." Default rule: "**export must stay within the customer's chosen region** that matches the deployment region." (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2)

**Exception path**: "If the customer cannot satisfy the above controls (e.g., insists on long-lived keys), file a Security exception under `security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions` and link it in the enablement ticket." (`customer-managed-audit-log-export-controls` §2)

**Execution routing** (`audit-log-export-request-intake` §2): "After approvals: Hosted: route to Eng Platform oncall / platform ops; Dedicated: route to Eng Infra; Private: route to Private Deployments engineering (and the customer's operator)."

## Answer

The complete gate is defined by **`private-upgrades-go-no-go-checklist-enterprise`** ("Private Deployments: Upgrade Go/No-Go Checklist (Enterprise)"), which is explicitly an *operational gate* that delegates the approval and comms specifics to four policy pages — all of which are in this corpus. Combined, the mandated gate is:

> "This checklist is the required go/no-go gate for upgrading an *enterprise* Redwood Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). It defines the minimum validations, evidence, and sign-offs required before starting the maintenance window, and the stop/rollback criteria during execution." — `private-upgrades-go-no-go-checklist-enterprise` · §2 · p1

> "Policy dependencies: This page is the operational gate, but approvals/comms requirements are defined in the Change Management Policy and Planned Maintenance Comms SOP. Security-specific sign-off requirements are defined in Secure SDLC: Security Sign-off for Customer Deployments. SLO/error budget checks are defined in Planned Change SLO / Error Budget Review Requirements." — same doc · §2 · p1

---

### 1. Required validations — pre-window ("must be complete 24h before window", §2 · p1–2)

- **A) Change record + ownership** — change request ticket from the *Private Upgrade Change Request* template (Jira internal-support); a single named **Change Owner**; confirmed customer-side **Change Approver** and **Operator** contacts.
- **B) Version + compatibility** — record current installer/operator/controller/runtime/chart versions; confirm target versions and exact upgrade path ("no skipping major versions unless explicitly supported"); confirm model/runtime compatibility for the customer's pinned models.
- **C) Backups + rollback readiness** — recent backups of control-plane config state, Redwood-managed PVs, documented customer external deps (DB, SSO, KMS); "Validate rollback artifacts are available locally: previous installer bundle, previous image tags, and prior values files"; an explicit rollback decision point in the window plan.
- **D) Preflight validations (attach evidence)** — cluster capacity/node readiness, storage class/PV health, DNS + egress reachability, TLS/cert expiry, "Required Kubernetes API versions present (no deprecated APIs that will break charts)".
- **E) Observability readiness** — dashboards/alerts visible to Redwood during the window (temporary access granted if needed), with control-plane API error rate, inference 5xx, P95 latency, GPU utilization/OOM/restart rates available.

### 2. The gate itself — at window start (§3 · p2)

> "The Change Owner must explicitly record "GO" in the change ticket after confirming all items below."

**1) Required sign-offs (links required)**
- "Change Management approvals completed (see policy for approvers by risk level)."
- "SRE SLO/error budget review completed (or documented risk acceptance)."
- "Security sign-off completed if triggered (auth/RBAC/audit/TLS/dependency changes)."
- "Customer Success owner acknowledges comms plan and customer readiness."

**2) Customer communications ready**
- "Maintenance notice sent according to comms SOP (timing + channel)."
- "During-window escalation path confirmed (Redwood + customer)."
- "\u201cAll clear\u201d message drafted for post-window."

**3) Final technical readiness**
- "Preflight output has no *red* blockers; any *yellow* warnings have an owner and mitigation."
- "No open P0/P1 incidents on Redwood side that would reduce ability to respond/rollback."
- "If a change freeze is active, an exception is approved and linked."

### 3. Approvals mandated by the Change Management Policy (`production-change-management-policy`)

The policy applies to "Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments (including customer-managed clusters)" (§3 · p1) and lists "upgrades to customer production Private clusters" among its risk-classification examples (§4 · p1). Its **Approval matrix (minimum approvers)** (§4 · p1):
- **Low** — "Engineering peer approval OR team lead approval." / "Owning team lead"
- **High** — "Owning team lead; SRE approver (named individual); Customer Success approver if customer-facing; Security approver if security triggers are met"
- **Critical** — "Director-level engineering approver; SRE approver; Security & Compliance approver; Customer Success approver" (§5 · p2)

**Go/No-Go gate requirement** (§5 · p2): "For High/Critical changes, the Change Owner must explicitly record a GO/NO-GO decision at window start including: Confirmation approvals are complete / Confirmation rollback is ready / Confirmation monitoring is in place / Confirmation customer comms are sent and acknowledged where applicable."
**Exceptions**: "Exceptions (including change freeze overrides) require explicit approval and must be linked from the change record." (§5 · p2)

**SRE review triggers** (§5 · p2): scaling/autoscaling/load-shedding changes; core request routing, fallback or region capacity; alerting changes or disabling alerts; "any planned downtime or performance regression risk."
**Security triggers** (§5 · p2): auth/SSO/token validation/signing keys/session handling; RBAC defaults or privileged service accounts; TLS/cert automation/trust stores; audit logging pipeline/retention/integrity; "Introduction of new third-party dependencies/images"; network boundaries (ingress/egress).

**SRE GO criteria** (`planned-change-slo-error-budget-review` · §2 · p1): review required for "any change that is classified Medium/High/Critical risk under the Production Change Management Policy, or any change that: Requires a maintenance window / Requires disabling alerts / Has a credible risk of increased 5xx, latency regression, or capacity shortfall". Required checks: 30-day error budget remaining ("If error budget remaining is below 25%, attach an explicit risk acceptance from Engineering + SRE lead"), capacity headroom (GPU + queue), monitoring/alert routing to active on-call, rollback feasibility within the customer "time-to-restore" target with a named decision point, and change-overlap check. "SRE will recommend GO only if: Rollback plan is concrete and feasible / Error budget is healthy or risk acceptance is documented / Monitoring is ready and on-call coverage confirmed / Customer comms plan exists when customer-visible."

**Security sign-off** (`security-signoff-customer-deployments` · §2 · p1): required for changes that (1) introduce/change authN/authZ (SSO, JWT validation, mTLS, service-to-service auth), (2) change RBAC defaults/scopes/privileged service accounts, (3) change audit logging behavior/retention/schemas/delivery guarantees, (4) change cryptographic material handling (key rotation, KMS/HSM, cert management), (5) "Introduce new third-party images/dependencies into the customer environment", (6) change network boundaries affecting exfiltration controls. Required artifacts: change summary, security-relevant config diff, dependency/image list with digests + provenance, vulnerability scan summary, audit-logging impact statement, rollback plan with time to restore prior security posture. Evidence of approval must record approver name, date/time, artifact links, and conditions; outcomes are "Approved / Approved with conditions / Not approved (rework required)"; SLA is "Standard review: 2 business days", expedited (<48h window) "requires S&C on-call approval and explicit risk acceptance from Engineering owner."

### 4. Required customer communications (`planned-maintenance-comms-sop-enterprise`)

"This SOP defines required customer and internal communications for planned maintenance affecting production workloads, **including Redwood Private upgrades**." (§2 · p1) **Required communications (minimum)**:
1. **Pre-notice (T-5 business days recommended; minimum T-48h for enterprise)** — "Send a maintenance notice to the customer via the agreed channel (usually email + shared Slack Connect if available)", including date/time window in the customer's timezone, expected impact (downtime vs degraded; which routes/models), expected downtime, required customer participation, "Rollback posture (we will rollback if KPIs exceed thresholds)", and link to the change record.
2. **Internal heads-up (T-48h)** — note in `#eng-oncall` and `#customer-success` with window time, customer name, change owner, "Whether a security sign-off is required", required customer participation (smoke tests, approvals, access), and Redwood escalation contacts.
3. **Window start (T=0)** — "Send a starting now message to the customer and internal channels. Confirm the backout plan exists and the next update time."
4. **Progress updates** — "Default cadence: every 30 minutes during the window"; "Immediate updates for any rollback or risk escalation".
5. **All-clear (post-window)** — "Send an all-clear message when the verification window is complete", with completed work summary, follow-ups, and post-change monitoring plan (e.g., 24h heightened watch).

Plus: "**Customer Success must approve customer-facing maintenance notices for enterprise accounts.**" (§2 · p2) and, for Private specifically, "do not post customer-specific maintenance on the public status page. Use direct customer comms unless contractually required otherwise." (§2 · p1). The Change Management Policy mirrors this: for customer-visible changes the record must include "Customer notification timing and channel / Internal comms plan (who is on bridge, where to post updates) / An all-clear message plan" (§5 · p2).

### 5. In-window stop points, rollback triggers, and evidence (§3 · p2–3)

- **Gate A (post-control-plane, within 10 min)**: operator/controller pods Ready; control-plane API healthy (no sustained 5xx); no unexpected restart loops.
- **Gate B (post-data-plane, within 15 min)**: runtime pods Ready and stable (no crashloops); synthetic inference request succeeds on each region/cluster segment; "Customer confirms application-level smoke test passes".
- **Gate C (verification window)**: "Hold for 30 minutes of steady state with alerting enabled and monitored."
- **Rollback criteria (immediate NO-GO / trigger rollback)**: sustained inference 5xx above customer baseline +5% for >5 min; P95 latency regression >30% for >10 min on primary routes; authentication (SSO/JWT) failures or RBAC denial spikes; audit log pipeline breaks (if contractual); "Control plane cannot reconcile/upgrade further".
- **Evidence to attach to the change record**: preflight output; version matrix (from/to); rollback plan (commands + expected time); "Links to SLO/error budget check and any risk acceptance"; "Security sign-off (or \u201cnot required\u201d rationale)"; "Copy of customer comms and confirmation of receipt".

**In one sentence:** an enterprise Private upgrade may only start when, ≥24h ahead, all five pre-window validation blocks (change record/ownership, version compatibility, backups + rollback artifacts, preflight evidence, observability) are complete; at window start the Change Owner records an explicit "GO" after confirming (a) Change Management approvals for the change's risk tier (owning team lead + named SRE approver + Customer Success approver for customer-facing + Security/Compliance approver when security triggers fire; Director-level engineering approver at Critical), SRE SLO/error-budget review (or documented risk acceptance), and security sign-off if triggered; (b) the comms SOP's notice was sent on the agreed channel and acknowledged, escalation paths are confirmed, and the all-clear is drafted, with Customer Success having approved the customer-facing notice; and (c) preflight has no red blockers, no Redwood P0/P1 incidents, and any change-freeze exception is approved and linked — then passing Gates A/B/C in-window and honoring the stated rollback triggers.

## Redwood Inference — End‑to‑End Production Change Process (Hosted API & Console)

The controlling policy is **`production-change-management-standard-v2`** ("Production Change Management Standard (v2)"), which both deploy runbooks and the gates page explicitly reference. It is executed through four operational pages: `prod-deployment-gates-hosted-api-console`, `hosted-api-deploy-runbook`, `console-deploy-runbook`, and `rollback-and-post-change-validation`.

---

### 1. Definition & scope — is this a production change?

**§4 Scope** (`production-change-management-standard-v2`):
> "Applies to all production environments for the Hosted API and Console, including: * Hosted API control plane and data plane services * Console UI and backend * Shared platform dependencies (routing, auth, billing metering, observability agents)"
> "Out of scope: customer-managed environments for *Private deployments* (see the Private Deployment Change Policy), and vendor-managed changes outside Redwood's control (cloud provider maintenance)."

**§5 Definitions**:
> "* *Production:* Any environment serving external customer traffic (including canary and regional production)."
> "* *Production change:* Any change that can affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, latency, cost, or correctness for customer-facing workloads."
> "* *Change owner:* The person accountable for end-to-end execution and follow-through."
> "* *Change record:* A durable record (ticket + links) capturing intent, risk, approvals, execution, and validation results."

**§7 What counts as a production change**:
> "Any deployment to production clusters (including canary regions) … Any change to routing policies, fallback policies, or model selection rules … Any change to auth, RBAC, API keys, rate limits, quotas, or billing meters … Any schema migration, backfill, or data retention configuration change … Any infrastructure change that affects capacity, autoscaling, or failover … Any change to observability pipelines that could reduce visibility (logs, metrics, tracing)"

The gates page scopes the same surface (`prod-deployment-gates-hosted-api-console` §4 "Applies to"): "Hosted API services (request router, inference gateway, streaming gateway, embeddings service, auth edge)", "Console services (console-web, console-api)", and "Shared dependencies when changed as part of a release (feature flags, policy configs)".

---

### 2. Required approvals (risk-tiered, role-based)

**§6 Change types and required approvals**:

| Change type | When used | Required approvals | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Emergency** | "Active incident mitigation or preventing imminent customer impact" | "On-call incident commander (IC) + service owner approval (as available)" | "Retrospective change record required within 24 hours" |
| **Standard** | "Low risk, pre-approved pattern (e.g., doc-only, internal dashboard query fixes, non-prod config)" | "1 peer approval" | "Must match an approved standard template" |
| **Normal** | "Most code/config deploys to production" | "1 peer approval + (1) service owner approval" | "Requires pre-deploy verification, canary, and comms assessment" |

**§10 Approvals**:
> "* *Peer approval:* A reviewer from the same engineering org who is familiar with the subsystem. * *Service owner approval:* The tech lead or on-call owner for the service being changed. * *SRE gate:* Required when the change affects capacity, SLO-sensitive paths, traffic routing, or any failover config. * *Security gate:* Required when the change touches auth, secrets, encryption, audit logging, PII, or data retention."

**§9 Risk assessment checklist** escalates tier: "If "yes" to any of 1–4, the change is *Normal* at minimum and may require Security Review (see Secure SDLC requirements)" — items cover auth/data paths/encryption/logging/retention; routing, batching, caching, model version selection; token accounting/billing; data migration/backfill. Item 5 asks "Is rollback fast and safe (< 10 minutes) and does it revert the customer experience?"

**§8 Minimum required artifacts** — every change needs a change record containing: "Summary of change and customer impact assessment", "Rollback plan (explicitly stated, even if "re-deploy previous build")", "Verification plan (how we will know it worked)", "Links to: PR(s), build(s), dashboards, runbook used, and any migration plan", and "Approvals (captured in the change record)".

Emergency path detail (`emergency-production-change-policy` §7): "Approvals are *role-based* and can be granted in Slack in the incident channel, but must be copied into the EPC record afterwards."

**§11 Change windows and freezes**: "Default window: weekdays 09:00–16:00 local time for the primary owning team." / "Changes are prohibited during declared change freezes." / "Additional restrictions apply when error budgets are low."

---

### 3. Pre-deploy verification

**Standard §12 Execution requirements**: "All production changes must: 1. Use the documented runbook for the target system (Hosted API or Console). 2. Perform a canary rollout for traffic-bearing services unless explicitly exempted in the change record. 3. Confirm observability before and after (golden signals and specific dashboards). 4. Have a clearly defined rollback trigger and a "stop the line" principle."

**Gates — "Pre-deploy gates (all required unless explicitly exempted)"** (`prod-deployment-gates-hosted-api-console` §5):
> "1. *Unit tests:* Green CI for all touched packages. 2. *Integration tests:* Green for service-level integration suite; exceptions must be approved by service owner. 3. *Perf sanity:* If request path or caching/batching changed, run perf-canary baseline or attach a prior comparable run. 4. *SLO posture:* Confirm current p95 latency and error rate are within normal bounds for the region(s) being deployed. 5. *Capacity posture:* If changing concurrency, batching, autoscaling, or kernel settings, confirm headroom ≥ 20% in target regions or include an SRE-approved plan. 6. *Schema/migration gate:* Any schema migration must be backward compatible and have a documented rollback/forward plan. 7. *Security gate:* Required when any of auth/RBAC/secrets/audit logging/PII retention is touched."

Required release artifacts (§5): "Link to change record (ticket)", "Link to PR(s) and test results", "Build identifier (image digest and/or build number)", "Release notes snippet (even internal-only)".

**Hosted API preconditions** (`hosted-api-deploy-runbook` §5): "1. A change record exists and includes summary, risk assessment, verification plan, and rollback plan." / "2. Approvals are captured (peer + service owner; add SRE/security as required)." / "3. CI is green; image digests are pinned (no "latest" tags)." Then §2 Pre-deploy checks: "Check current error rates and p95 latency dashboards for the target services."

**Console preconditions** (`console-deploy-runbook` §5): "1. Change record exists with rollback + verification plans. 2. Approvals captured (peer + service owner; add security review if auth/session handling changes). 3. Release artifact prepared: build IDs for console-web and console-api. 4. If UI copy changes could confuse customers, prepare comms text for Support (internal)." §2 Pre-deploy checks: "Confirm console-api error rate and p95 latency are within baseline. / Confirm auth provider status is healthy (if applicable). / Confirm no active incidents affecting login/session."

---

### 4. Deploy execution (canary → full)

**Canary policy** (`prod-deployment-gates-hosted-api-console` §6):
> "Canary is mandatory for traffic-bearing services unless the change is doc-only or explicitly exempted."
> "* Canary scope: 1 region OR 1% traffic (whichever is supported by the service) * Canary duration: minimum 15 minutes of steady-state traffic * Canary pass criteria: - Error rate does not regress by > 0.2% absolute - p95 latency does not regress by > 10% - No sustained saturation signals (GPU queue depth, CPU throttling, memory pressure)"

**Hosted API** (`hosted-api-deploy-runbook`): "Deployment mode: canary then full" (§6). §3 Canary deploy: "Deploy to canary region (default us-west-2) or 1% traffic slice if supported", using e.g. `deployctl status --service inference-gateway --env prod --region us-west-2` and `deployctl promote --service inference-gateway --env prod --region us-west-2 --image-digest sha256:...`. §4 "Canary validation (15 minutes minimum)": "Validate: error rate, p95 latency, saturation signals, and request timeouts." §5 Full rollout: "If canary passes criteria, deploy remaining regions in order: us-east-1 -> eu-central-1." / "Deploy one region at a time; do not run concurrent region rollouts for router + gateway changes unless explicitly approved."

**Console** (`console-deploy-runbook` §6 Deployment approach): "Prefer: deploy console-api first, then console-web. / Use feature flags to dark-launch new features; avoid releasing a UI that depends on a backend not yet deployed. / Canary: enable for internal staff cohort before broad release when feasible." §3 Deploy console-api: "Deploy to production using deployctl with pinned image digest. / Validate readiness and basic health endpoint." §4 Canary validation: "Validate login, org switching, API key creation, usage dashboard loads, and a representative settings page. / Confirm feature-flag evaluations are succeeding; check for increased 401/403." §5 Deploy console-web: "Publish the new static bundle and confirm cache invalidation completes. / Keep prior bundle available for rapid rollback."

---

### 5. Customer and internal communications

**Standard §13 Communications requirements**:
> "Change owner must determine if customer communications are required: See "Planned Maintenance and Change Communications" for templates and required lead time. * *Planned maintenance:* Status page notice and direct customer comms if any material impact is expected. * *No expected customer impact:* Internal announcement in #eng-releases and on-call awareness if during core hours."

**Internal announcements**: Hosted API runbook — "Post in #eng-releases with: change record link, services, canary region, start time, rollback trigger." Console runbook §1 "Announce (internal)" — "Post in #eng-releases: change record, affected components, start time, canary plan, rollback trigger." Escalation contacts: "On-call escalation: #eng-oncall and #eng-platform".

---

### 6. Rollback and post-change requirements

**Standard §14 Post-change validation and closure**:
> "Within 60 minutes after completion, the change owner must: * Validate key SLO metrics and error rates are within normal bounds * Confirm canary is healthy before full rollout * Update the change record with results and attach screenshots/links * File follow-ups for any issues discovered"

**Post-deploy gates** (`prod-deployment-gates-hosted-api-console` §7):
> "1. *Verify functional health:* key endpoints return expected responses (smoke tests). 2. *Verify observability:* dashboards show data, alerts are not muted unexpectedly, and logs can be queried. 3. *Verify billing/usage integrity:* if metering touched, validate token counts on a test account and at least one production cohort. 4. *Watch window:* maintain enhanced monitoring for 60 minutes after full rollout."

Required dashboards: "Hosted API: Request success rate, p50/p95 latency, token throughput, saturation (GPU/CPU), router 5xx by route"; "Console: Web error rate, console-api 5xx, auth failures, UI load time, feature-flag evaluation errors". Exemptions only when "The change is truly non-impacting to production behavior / The exemption is documented in the change record / The service owner approves the exemption".

**Rollback** (`rollback-and-post-change-validation`):
- §6 Rollback decision criteria: "Rollback immediately if: * Canary or post-deploy gates fail (error/latency regression beyond thresholds) * Data correctness, billing, auth, or routing correctness is in question * New Sev2+ customer impact appears plausibly correlated"
- §7 Rollback steps (generic): "1. Stop further rollout — Pause deployments and disable automated promotions." → "2. Revert highest-leverage toggles first — Disable or revert feature flags / routing policy bundles associated with the change." → "3. Redeploy prior build — Redeploy the previous image digest to the impacted region(s). For Hosted API, roll back region-by-region starting with the canary/most impacted region." → "4. Validate health — Confirm service readiness and key smoke tests pass." → "5. Document — Update change record with: trigger, rollback start/end time, and final state."
- §13 Special cases: "* Schema migrations: If a forward-only migration was applied, rollback may require a compensating forward fix rather than reverting binaries. Always involve the service owner and SRE on-call." / "* Auth/RBAC changes: Validate both positive and negative authorization outcomes after rollback."
- §16 Post-change monitoring window (required): "For any production change (successful or rolled back): * Enhanced monitoring for at least 60 minutes after the system is stable. * Confirm: error rate, p95 latency, saturation metrics, and a representative customer workflow."
- §17 Closure requirements: "A change record is not closed until it includes: * Final deployed build identifiers (or confirmation of rollback) * Links to dashboards used and observed outcomes * Follow-up tickets for any discovered issues"

**Runbook quick paths**: Hosted API — "Use the previous known-good image digest and redeploy to the impacted region(s). If the router policy config changed, revert the config bundle first. Follow the dedicated Rollback and Post-change Validation runbook for full steps and post-rollback monitoring." Console — "console-web: revert to prior bundle and re-run cache invalidation. console-api: redeploy prior image digest. Feature flags: disable the newly launched flag(s) first if they are implicated." Closeout in both runbooks: "Update the change record with: canary results, rollout times, dashboard links, and final build identifiers."

---

## Concise answer

Redwood's process is: **(1) Classify** — anything that can affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, latency, cost, or correctness of customer-facing Hosted API/Console workloads (including canary regions, routing, auth/RBAC, quotas, billing meters, migrations, capacity, observability) is a production change. **(2) Record** — the change owner opens a durable change record with summary + customer impact, risk assessment, verification plan, explicit rollback plan, and links to PRs/builds/dashboards/runbook. **(3) Approve** — Standard = 1 peer; Normal = 1 peer + service owner; Emergency = incident commander + service owner (as available) with a retrospective record within 24 hours; plus an SRE gate for capacity/SLO/routing/failover and a Security gate for auth/secrets/encryption/audit/PII/retention; only in the weekday 09:00–16:00 window and never during a freeze. **(4) Verify pre-deploy** — green unit/integration tests, perf sanity if the request path changed, SLO posture in bounds, ≥20% capacity headroom, backward-compatible migration with rollback plan, security gate cleared, pinned image digests (no "latest"), and baseline error-rate/p95 dashboards checked. **(5) Execute** — follow the Hosted API or Console runbook: announce, then canary (1 region or 1% traffic, minimum 15 minutes steady state) against pass criteria (error rate not worse by >0.2% absolute, p95 not worse by >10%, no sustained saturation), then full rollout region-by-region (Hosted API: us-west-2 → us-east-1 → eu-central-1; Console: console-api first, then console-web, dark-launched behind feature flags). **(6) Communicate** — internal post in #eng-releases with change record, services/canary region, start time and rollback trigger (plus #eng-oncall/#eng-platform escalation); customer-facing status page notice and direct comms for planned maintenance with material impact. **(7) Validate, roll back, close** — within 60 minutes validate SLO metrics/error rates, canary health, functional smoke tests, observability, and billing integrity; roll back immediately if canary/post-deploy gates fail or data/billing/auth/routing correctness is in question by stopping rollout, reverting flags/policy bundles, redeploying the prior digest region-by-region, validating health, and documenting trigger/times/final state; enhanced monitoring for at least 60 minutes after stability for successful *and* rolled-back changes; the record cannot be closed until it has final build identifiers (or rollback confirmation), dashboard links with observed outcomes, and follow-up tickets.
